title: 中国人怎么吃一条鱼①松鼠桂鱼：一条鱼划128刀，炸出一只"松鼠" | How China Eats a Fish P1 · Suzhou Squirrel Fish 🐟
description:
先赏形，还是先动筷？你会怎么吃这条"松鼠"？

《中国人怎么吃一条鱼》第一集：苏州松鼠桂鱼。最见功夫的一点——整条鳜鱼要在鱼身上斜剞菱形花刀，横八刀、竖八刀，划出上百个棱，却刀刀断肉不断骨。拍上淀粉下滚油，鱼肉遇热瞬间翻卷开花，头昂尾翘，活脱一只松鼠。相传乾隆下江南到松鹤楼，想尝供在神台的"元宝鱼"，厨师怕担杀"神鱼"之罪，便把它改做成松鼠形——糖醋滚汁一浇，滋滋作响，那声音真像松鼠在叫。松鹤楼创于清乾隆二十二年（1757年），这道菜至今已有两百多年。（乾隆典故为民间相传，如实标注。）

How China eats a fish, Part 1: Suzhou squirrel mandarin fish. The craft is all in the knife — a whole mandarin fish scored eight cuts down and eight across into a hundred-plus diamonds, every cut through the flesh but never the bone. Dusted in starch and dropped in hot oil, the flesh blooms open, head high and tail curled, into the shape of a squirrel. Legend says the Qianlong Emperor wanted the "sacred fish" from the altar, so a Songhelou chef disguised it as a squirrel; when the hot sweet-and-sour sauce hits, it sizzles like a squirrel's squeak. Songhelou opened in 1757; the dish is over two centuries old. (The Qianlong story is folk legend, noted as such.)
